paramount

PAIR-uh-mount — contains 'mount,' like a mountain peak standing above all else. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Paramount is more important than anything else.

In any hospital emergency room, patient safety is paramount.

Example

Before a rocket launch, engineers check the weather, the fuel levels, and dozens of backup systems. Because safety is paramount, if even one check fails, the entire launch is stopped, no matter the cost or the schedule.

Nothing — not cost, not schedule — is allowed to outweigh safety here. Unlike 'important,' which allows for several equally important things, paramount specifically means one concern outranks every other.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

supreme: Supreme means highest in rank or power — a supreme court, a supreme ruler holds the top position itself. Paramount is about priority in a decision: the paramount concern is the one that outweighs every other consideration, whoever holds the power.

foremost: Foremost means standing at the front of a list — the foremost expert, the foremost example, the first name people mention. Paramount is stronger: a paramount concern does not just lead the list, it outweighs everything else on it.

chief: Chief flags the main one among several — the chief reason, the chief engineer. Calling a concern paramount goes further: it is not merely first among the considerations but so important that every other one must give way to it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

minor: of little importance

secondary: of lesser importance than something else

Where it sits · how high it ranks in importance

significant → paramount → sacred

significant vs. paramount: Significant is weaker than paramount — a significant concern matters, but a paramount one outranks every single other concern entirely.

sacred vs. paramount: Sacred can be stronger than paramount: a paramount concern is simply the most important one, but something sacred must never be compromised under any circumstances at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mont-: mountain, to climb (Latin (via Anglo-Norman 'amont,' upward))

Put it together: Paramount comes from Anglo-Norman paramont, built from par (by) plus amont (upward), itself from Latin ad montem, 'to the mountain.' Something paramount is figuratively above everything else, like standing at the mountain's peak.

Use the root in a new word: surmount: The team had to surmount several setbacks before finally finishing the project on time.
